definitions.explanation: Knowledge or insights gained through experience, research, or study. Often implies practical, specialized knowledge that has been accumulated over time.

examples.japanese: {専門的|せんもんてき}な{知見|ちけん}を{活|い}かす。
examples.english: To make use of specialized knowledge.

examples.japanese: この{分野|ぶんや}の{知見|ちけん}が{不足|ふそく}している。
examples.english: Knowledge in this field is lacking.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{研究|けんきゅう}で{得|え}られた{知見|ちけん}を、{次|つぎ}の{世代|せだい}に{伝|つた}えていくことが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: It is important to pass on the knowledge gained through years of research to the next generation.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal word commonly used in academic, business, and technical contexts. Often appears in the pattern {知見|ちけん}を{得|え}る (to gain knowledge), {知見|ちけん}を{共有|きょうゆう}する (to share knowledge/findings), or {知見|ちけん}を{活|い}かす (to apply knowledge). More formal and specialized than {知識|ちしき} (general knowledge).

WRITING:
{知|ち} means "to know" and {見|けん} means "to see" or "view." The compound suggests knowledge gained through observation and experience.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {知識|ちしき}: knowledge (general, broader)
- {知見|ちけん}: knowledge, findings (specialized, from experience/research)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {知見|ちけん}を{得|え}る: to gain knowledge/findings
- {知見|ちけん}を{活|い}かす: to apply knowledge
- {知見|ちけん}を{共有|きょうゆう}する: to share findings
- {知見|ちけん}を{蓄積|ちくせき}する: to accumulate knowledge
